info.title: Torq API (baton-torq connector surface)
info.description:
This document describes ONLY the Torq API surface that the baton-torq connector calls. It is not a full description of Torq's public API. Scope was derived from pkg/torq/client.go (request sites) and settled against Torq's public API docs at https://developers.torq.io/apidocs (accessed 2026-10-01).

The connector talks to two hosts:
- The data API host (regional, configurable) for /users and /users/roles.
- A fixed auth host for the OAuth2 client-credentials token exchange.

Base URL / region: the connector's compiled-in default data API base URL is `https://api.torq.io/public/v1alpha/` (see pkg/torq/client.go:16, `DefaultBaseURL`). It can be overridden via the `base-url` connector config field (pkg/config/config.go:25, hidden/CLI-only `--base-url` flag, described as "Override the Torq API URL (for testing)"). An operator can point this at Torq's EU host (`https://api.eu.torq.io/...`) to target an EU workspace; the connector itself does not auto-detect region.

Discrepancy worth flagging: Torq's public docs (developers.torq.io) describe the data API paths as `https://api.torq.io/v1alpha/users` and `https://api.torq.io/v1alpha/users/roles` (no `/public` path segment), while the connector's compiled-in default base URL includes `/public/v1alpha/`. This spec models the connector's actual runtime behavior (base URL + relative paths exactly as `pkg/torq/client.go` constructs them via `url.JoinPath`), not the vendor docs' literal path. Unverified which of the two is authoritative for the production API; see PR description.

servers.description: Default Torq data API base URL (US region), as compiled into pkg/torq/client.go (DefaultBaseURL). Overridable via the connector's `base-url` config field (hidden/CLI-only --base-url flag) -- e.g. to `https://api.eu.torq.io/public/v1alpha` for an EU-region workspace. Used by the /users and /users/roles operations.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Client-credentials token exchange. Fixed host, not covered by the `base-url` override.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Operations backing the connector's user sync.

tags.name: Roles
tags.description: Operations backing the connector's role sync and role-membership grants.

post.summary: Exchange client credentials for a bearer access token
post.description:
Called once per connector run from pkg/torq/client.go RequestAccessToken (client.go:40-75) to obtain the bearer token used to authenticate every subsequent request to the data API. Not affected by the `base-url` config field -- the host is hardcoded in the connector as `https://auth.torq.io`.

Vendor docs also list a regional EU auth host, `https://auth.eu.torq.io/v1/auth/token`, for workspaces on the eu.torq.io domain, but this connector has no config field to select it; RequestAccessToken always targets the US host.

servers.description: Fixed Torq auth host used by RequestAccessToken (client.go:46). Not configurable via `base-url`. Vendor also publishes https://auth.eu.torq.io for EU-domain workspaces (unused by this connector).

200.description: A successful response containing the bearer access token.

401.description: Invalid client ID or client secret. Documented by the vendor (developers.torq.io/apidocs/authentication); the connector does not parse this response body, it only checks for a non-2xx status code (client.go:65-67).

get.description: Called twice per connector sync from pkg/torq/client.go: once by listLocalUsers (client.go:78-89), with the `sso_provision` query parameter omitted, and once by listSsoUsers (client.go:92-105), with `sso_provision=true` hardcoded. The public ListUsers method (client.go:108-124) concatenates both result sets. Also exercised by Connector.Validate (pkg/connector/connector.go:37-43) as the credential-validation probe.

parameters.name: sso_provision
parameters.description: Filters users by provisioning method. The connector hardcodes this to `true` in listSsoUsers (client.go:99) to fetch SSO-provisioned users, and omits it entirely in listLocalUsers (client.go:83-84) to fetch the rest. Vendor docs state omitting it returns locally-provisioned users and that explicit `false` is equivalent to that same local-user behavior; the connector itself never sends `sso_provision=false` explicitly, only omits the parameter -- unverified whether that is identical to all-users or locally-provisioned-only on the vendor side.

get.summary: List roles that can be assigned to users in the workspace
get.description: Called from pkg/torq/client.go ListRoles (client.go:127-146), driven by pkg/connector/roles.go roleBuilder.List (roles.go:52-80) via the SDK's bag-based pagination token.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Cursor from a previous List roles response's `next_page_token`. The connector always sends this parameter (client.go:133-134), including an empty string on the first page of a sync. The connector never sets `page_size`, so the vendor's default page size (50, max 100 per vendor docs) applies.

basicAuth.description: HTTP Basic auth using the Torq API key (client_id as username, client_secret as password). See pkg/torq/client.go:47, torq-client-id / torq-client-secret config fields (pkg/config/config.go:10-23).

bearerAuth.description: Bearer token obtained from POST /v1/auth/token (requestAccessToken) and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every data-API request. See pkg/torq/client.go:158-159.

AuthTokenRequest.description: Form-encoded body sent by RequestAccessToken (client.go:48-50). The connector only ever sends the client_credentials grant.

AuthResponse.description: Response of the token endpoint, as decoded by pkg/torq/client.go AuthResponse struct (client.go:18-21). Torq's response also includes `expires_in` and `token_type` (confirmed via vendor docs sample response), but the connector does not read either field, so they are omitted here per the connector's actual struct.

access_token.description: Bearer token used for subsequent data-API requests.

ListUsersResponse.description: Envelope decoded by listLocalUsers/listSsoUsers (client.go:79-81, 93-95) as an anonymous `struct { Users []User "json:\"users\"" }`.

User.description: Fields match pkg/torq/models.go User struct (models.go:3-9) exactly. Vendor docs (developers.torq.io/apidocs/list-users) additionally document created_time and last_login_time on this object; both are omitted here because the connector's struct does not declare them. Per the vendor's raw schema metadata, none of these fields are marked required in the response -- all are modeled as optional here.

id.description: The unique identifier of the user. Used by the connector as the resource ID and (via WithExternalID-equivalent identity) for role-grant matching against Role.ID.

email.description: The user's email address. Used as the resource display name and UserTrait email.

role_id.description: The unique identifier of the role assigned to the user. Matched against Role.ID in roleBuilder.Grants (pkg/connector/roles.go:100-118).

status.description: VERIFIED maps to v2.UserTrait_Status_STATUS_ENABLED; STATUS_UNSPECIFIED and INVITATION_SENT both map to v2.UserTrait_Status_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED in pkg/connector/users.go:34-42 (no connector-side status exists for INVITATION_SENT).

sso_provision.description: True if the user was provisioned via SSO. Surfaced in the resource profile as `sso_provisioned`.

ListRolesResponse.description: Envelope decoded by ListRoles (client.go:128-131) as an anonymous `struct { Roles []Role "json:\"roles\""; NextPageToken string "json:\"next_page_token,omitempty\"" }`.

next_page_token.description: Pagination cursor. Per vendor docs: present only when another page of results exists; its absence/empty value terminates the connector's pagination loop (client.go:141-145: `if res.NextPageToken != "" { return res.Roles, res.NextPageToken, nil }; return res.Roles, "", nil`).

ErrorResponse.description: Default/error envelope documented by the vendor for 401/403/default responses on the data API (developers.torq.io/apidocs/list-users raw schema, accessed 2026-10-01). The connector does not parse this body; it is documented here for completeness only, not because client.go reads it.

Role.description: Fields match pkg/torq/models.go Role struct (models.go:11-15) exactly. Vendor docs additionally document a `scope_names` array on this object; it is omitted here because the connector's struct does not declare it. Per the vendor's raw schema metadata, none of these fields are marked required in the response -- all are modeled as optional here.

id.description: The unique identifier of the role. Used as the role resource ID and matched against User.RoleID.

name.description: The name of the role. Used as the role resource display name.

description.description: The description of the role. Surfaced in the resource profile as `role_description`.
